name: js-harness-r2
goal: Finish the JS harness. Round 1 accepted the lexer, import scanner and TAP parser; the export reader never got a word written (Barry's model returned HTTP 500s and timeouts), which blocked the gate. The lexer also has to learn regex literals: the gate misread a real module because a quote inside /"/g looked like a string.

tasks.instructions: You wrote the first version of this module and it passed. The contract now has a fifth kind, 'regex' (rule 5), because a real module was misjudged: in s.replace(/"/g, """) the quote inside the regex was read as the start of a string, and everything after it was mis-segmented. Keep every earlier rule and table row passing. Track what came before each '/' in code (ignoring comments); a string, template or regex before it counts as a value.
tasks.test_instructions: Cover rule 5 from both sides: a '/' that must be a regex (after '(', '=', 'return', at the very start) and one that must be division (after a name, after ')', after a string). Include a '/' inside a character class and a regex interrupted by a newline. Keep the round-trip rule tested.

tasks.instructions: You MUST import the accepted js_lex module (from js_lex import code_only). The hard part is stub_functions: default parameters contain braces and parentheses, so match the parameter list and the body by counting depth, never by searching for the first '}'. Do not write docstrings that explain reasons the contract does not give.
tasks.test_instructions: Test each of the six export rules separately, and for stubs include a default parameter with braces, a nested throw that is NOT a stub, and a throw with a computed message that is NOT a stub. Cover every numbered rule; an earlier crew test file left two stated rules untested.

tasks.instructions: You MUST import the three accepted modules. Rule order is the whole point: run_tests must never be called when a static rule rejected the module. Build the result dict in one helper, not in five places.
tasks.test_instructions: Pass a run_tests that records its calls, and prove it is called zero times for every static rejection and exactly once otherwise. Test the rule-order case where a module is both unsafe and missing the API.
